md_south_west.blurb: South West is a short run of quartzite cliff on Cat Rock in Cunningham Falls State Park, in the Catoctin hills of western Maryland. Every line here is set up as a top rope, so it suits a day of ropes and slings rather than a rack. Grades stretch from very easy up to 5.10, with the bulk of the climbs between 5.7 and 5.10, which gives beginners and intermediate climbers something to do. The rock begins low near the overlook and grows taller as you work down and east along the band. Expect lichen in places and the odd loose block, and keep in mind that the whole outcrop is a hike in rather than a roadside crag.

md_sisters_corner_and_ampitheater_area.blurb: Sisters' Corner and the Amphitheater make up a stretch of quartzite wall on the north side of the Cumberland Narrows above the city of Cumberland, Maryland. The eleven routes here are all traditional leads, running from an easy 5.4 arete through the 5.7 to 5.8 range and up to a handful at 5.9 and 5.10. The Narrows cliff as a whole faces southwest, so it catches afternoon sun and can be very hot in summer. Bolts are scarce across the cliff, so plan to place your own gear and build anchors from trees. Thick leaf cover can make finding the start of a route slow, and the base collects some litter thrown from the road above.

md_cupids_bower.blurb: Cupids Bower is a small crag at the downstream end of Sherwin Island, on the Maryland side of the Potomac at Great Falls. It holds around ten routes, mostly trad with a top rope or two and a single boulder problem, spanning easy fifth class up to 5.12. Most of the climbing sits in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, so it leans toward experienced climbers. The wall stands back from the water in the trees instead of rising straight from the river, and the island is reached by crossing the river and following trails downstream. Expect scrambling and rough ground throughout this stretch of the gorge.

_expect.name: Blue Ridge Summit/Hog Rock Parking Boulders

md_blue_ridge_summit_hog_rock_parking_bo.blurb: This small cluster of boulders sits northwest of the Hog Rock parking area in Catoctin Mountain Park, near Thurmont in Maryland. It is a quick outing: the blocks are only a few hundred feet from the lot, though there is no built trail yet, so expect a short bushwhack through the woods. Eleven problems range from the easiest grades up to V8, with a cluster of hard lines around V7 and a few friendly ones in the V2 to V3 range. It makes a handy stop for a short session or a warm-up before heading to the larger boulder fields elsewhere in the park.

md_friction_wall.blurb: Friction Wall is an old quarry face in Patapsco Valley State Park near Ellicott City, Maryland. It is the park's tallest wall and its one spot with bolted sport lines, alongside a few trad routes and a top rope. The center is a clean slab, with an arete and a sport wall beside it; the right side is mossy and swampy and mostly used for aid. Eleven routes run from easy up to 5.12, with a bulge of lines in the 5.8 and 5.10 to 5.11 range, and the slab climbing rewards good footwork and finger strength. The top is badly eroded, so anchors are usually reached by rappelling from a tree.

md_north_bank_uphill_slab.blurb: Uphill Slab is a bouldering sector at Northwest Branch, a wooded stream corridor in Silver Spring, Maryland, just north of Washington, DC. It holds about a dozen problems, and the large majority are easy to moderate, between the lowest grades and V4, which suits footwork practice on the slab. A couple of much harder lines top out the range near V7 and V9. The boulders are a short walk on a maintained path from the car park, so the day is easy to plan. Bring a crash pad and a spotter, and be aware that hikers and bikers use the same corridor.
